title: QC configuration
purpose: Inspect seven types of laboratory configuration controlling preservation, independent preparation, calculated results, holding clocks, QC frequencies/limits and result qualifiers.
summary: See the lab's configured preservation rules, preparation requirements, calculation rules, holding-time rules, QC requirements, QC limits and result qualifiers. Only administrators can change them.

tasks.title: See one method's configuration
steps: Choose the [[Method]] and select [[Apply]]. Qualifiers are not filtered by method.

tasks.title: Add a rule, requirement, limit or qualifier
steps: Select the add button in that table's header, for example [[Add QC limit]], [[Add holding-time rule]] or [[Add calculation rule]].

tasks.title: Make a test calculated from readings
steps: In Calculation rules, select [[Add calculation rule]] and choose the test, the calculation, the rounding and the basis.
Save. Analysts then enter readings for that test instead of a final result.

tasks.title: Change a configured row
steps: Select the row's first cell to open its edit form. Only administrators see these as links.

good_to_know: These values are the lab's own policy, not regulatory defaults. The demonstration values are synthetic and not validated.
Missing configuration is never a pass. No QC limit means Not evaluated, and no holding rule means holding time is not evaluated.
Changes apply to new work. Results already entered and reports already issued keep the values they were made with.
Inactive rows stay listed so their history remains visible.
A calculation rule changes how manual results of one test are entered. Typed and imported results are never rounded, and worksheets already recorded keep the rule they were worked with.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: These are staff pages. Active users with an application staff role can read them; client accounts cannot. Analysts perform result entry and batch work, reviewers decide results, and administrators maintain configuration. Administrators also have operational analyst and reviewer access, but independence rules still apply. Superuser status alone does not grant an application role.

items.label: Method
items.description: All methods by default; choices include inactive method versions. Filters preservation rules, independent preparation requirements, calculation rules, holding rules, QC requirements and QC limits. It does not filter result qualifiers.

items.label: Apply
items.description: Apply the selected method across six tables. An invalid method shows an error and no rows in those six tables; qualifiers remain visible.

items.label: Clear all
items.description: Restore all methods.

items.label: Columns
items.description: Each table has its own browser-saved visibility/order dialog and Reset columns. Identifier columns stay available. These tables have no sortable header links.

items.label: Rows per page
items.description: Only QC limits are paginated: 25 by default, 50 or 100. Their page links retain the method filter. Other tables show their full selected sets.

items.label: Spreadsheet import
items.description: Administrators can also create or change QC requirements, holding-time rules, QC limits and preservation rules from CSV files under Setup → Spreadsheet import, with a row-by-row preview and the same checks and history as these forms. Preparation requirements, calculation rules and qualifiers are not imported.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact test definition (method/version, analyte and matrix); opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Temperature
items.description: Configured range with lower/upper/unit, No temperature requirement, or Manual temperature assessment.

items.label: Source / applicability
items.description: Method/SOP source and applicability text used in assessment evidence.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the rule is used in current screening.

items.label: Add preservation rule
items.description: Administrators create a rule for one exact test. No configured rule does not imply acceptance; chemical/container requirements remain manual.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact analytical test definition; opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Preparation method
items.description: Required exact preparation method/version for new observations.

items.label: Source / applicability
items.description: Laboratory source and applicability.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether new observations require an explicit prepared aliquot.

items.label: Add preparation requirement
items.description: Administrators link a test to its independent preparation method. No requirement does not establish that physical preparation is unnecessary.

sections.title: Calculation rules
paragraphs: A rule makes manual results of one test calculated from readings and sets how the calculated value is rounded. The readings, the calculation version and the rounding are kept with each result as a worksheet. Typed and imported results are never rounded, and file imports still supply final values. There is no default rounding: it is the laboratory's own rule, recorded with its basis. One rule can exist per test, so a test uses one calculation: it is either corrected to dry weight or not. The rounding also applies to a reporting limit that a preparation calculation works out.

With no rule, the test takes typed results as before. An empty table says that every result is typed or imported as a final value; a method filter with no match says there are no calculation rules for these filters and to clear the method filter.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact test definition (method/version, analyte and matrix); opens the edit form for administrators and is plain text for everyone else.

items.label: Calculation
items.description: The calculation and its current version, for example Solids by weight, balance in grams (version 1) or Prepared solid corrected to dry weight, mg/L in solution to mg/kg (version 1). A rule that names a calculation this release does not have shows Not in this release with its stored key; an administrator must change it, and entry of that test is refused until then.

items.label: Rounding
items.description: The laboratory's rounding in words: significant figures or decimal places, with the optional second rounding for larger values, and half to even or half up. For example 3 significant figures, half to even.

items.label: Source / applicability
items.description: The method or SOP basis recorded with the rule.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the rule currently applies. An inactive rule is ignored: the test takes typed results again, and worksheets already recorded stay.

items.label: Add calculation rule
items.description: Administrators create a rule for one exact test. Other staff do not see this action, and the empty state offers it to administrators only.

sections.title: Holding-time rules

items.label: Rule
items.description: Rule name; opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Method
items.description: Exact method/version.

items.label: Matrix
items.description: Water, Wastewater or Soil.

items.label: Applies to
items.description: All analytes for a method-wide rule, or the one analyte the rule is limited to.

items.label: From → to
items.description: Collection/composite end or Preparation start through Preparation start or Analysis start.

items.label: Maximum
items.description: Configured maximum duration; optional warning shows the remaining-time threshold.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the clock is applied to new evaluations.

items.label: Add holding-time rule
items.description: Administrators define an explicit clock for the whole method or for one analyte. No applicable active rule gives a not-evaluated holding status, not a fabricated threshold.

paragraphs: A rule applies to every analyte of its method and matrix unless it names one. A rule that names an analyte replaces the method-wide rule with the same start and end events for that analyte only; other clocks and other analytes are unaffected. Method-wide rules are listed before the analyte rules of the same clock.

items.label: Method
items.description: Exact method/version; opens that type’s requirement for administrators.

items.label: QC type
items.description: Configured QC sample type.

items.label: Minimum per batch
items.description: Minimum count for the type.

items.label: One per N samples
items.description: Optional additional sample-frequency count; required total is the greater of the minimum and rounded-up samples/N.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the frequency is enforced.

items.label: Add QC requirement
items.description: Administrators create a frequency requirement. With none configured, no QC sample frequency is enforced.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact definition; phase Analysis or Preparation appears beneath it. Opens edit for administrators.

items.label: QC type
items.description: Type whose measure is evaluated.

items.label: Measure
items.description: Measured value, Percent recovery or Relative percent difference.

items.label: Lower
items.description: Inclusive lower acceptance bound, or a dash if none.

items.label: Upper
items.description: Inclusive upper acceptance bound, or a dash if none.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether current QC evaluation uses the limit.

items.label: Add QC limit
items.description: Administrators create bounds for the exact test, phase, QC type and measure. Missing applicable limits produce Not evaluated and hold approval.

items.label: Code
items.description: Result qualifier code; opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Description
items.description: Meaning captured into a result revision when used.

items.label: Marks holding-time exceedance
items.description: Whether this qualifier can identify a result’s exceeded holding time for submission/review checks.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether new entries may select the code.

items.label: Add qualifier
items.description: Administrators define a code and meaning. Qualifiers are not filtered by method.

sections.title: Policy and history
paragraphs: Only administrators can save configuration. Existing edits require a reason, preserve before/after audit values and reject stale edit forms. Inactive rows remain listed. Configuration represents lab-owned policy, not regulatory defaults; synthetic seed values are not validated. Frozen result/report snapshots retain their earlier values, while current QC and preservation checks can change approval/release eligibility. Empty sections explain the consequence of absent configuration and offer Add controls to administrators.

sections.title: Titration calculations
paragraphs: Alkalinity by titration to pH 4.5, Low alkalinity by two-endpoint titration and Total hardness by EDTA titration produce mg/L as CaCO3. The test must use that exact unit and cannot be soil. The laboratory chooses the calculation per test; a result never switches the procedure automatically.

The three titration calculations retain burette readings, sample volume and actual standardized titrant normality. Alkalinity also keeps endpoint pH. They apply no dilution or blank correction and do not scale the reporting limit. The calculation rule form describes each equation and its limits.
